body:
Take a file fetch.js with content:
```js
fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
Executing with `bun run fetch.js` terminates without any logging while doing `deno run fetch.js` prints the actual content of the response.

Other problem, adding await in front of everything, like:
```js
await fetch("https://www.google.com/").then(x=>console.log(x));
```
prints
```
[0.05ms] "node_modules.bun" - 1 modules, 1 packages
[native code]
```
instead of the relevant response.

title: `fs/promises` support
Set-Cookie Headers behavior
body: The behavior of setting cookies with the `Headers` type does not allow you to set multiple cookies. See [this issue](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/1437) for undici (node's implementation of fetch) for what they might be doing about it. Deno seems to behave the way that will work with browsers (setting a new header entry for each set-cookie) and it seems like that's the only header that needs to behave that way, which is why it seems that `Headers.prototype.getSetCookie` is a proposal to solve for this issue.

title: Compatibility data mapping
body:
Is there a way to know a JavaScriptCore version (-> WebKit and Safari with the same engine version) for each current and future `bun` version? For example, for each NodeJS version, we can see the related V8 (-> Chrome) version [here](https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json). `process.versions.webkit` is just a hash:

```js
process.versions.webkit; // => 9a039f4901c48680700174c28dd4693873f7593a
```

Why it's required? To simplify getting compatibility data (sure, not for all) for `bun`. This data can be used by `core-js` and, for example, `babel` to include only required polyfills and transpile only unsupported features.

title: Slow down when use `await`
body: ### Version 0.1.1 ### Platform Darwin Salt.local 21.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.5.0: Tue Apr 26 21:08:37 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.121.3~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64 ### What steps will reproduce the bug? Bun is slowed down while using `await` keyword. TLDR; [Reproducible repo](https://github.com/SaltyAom/issue-bun-slow-async) In the real-world app, `async` is required (eg. querying from a database). However, using it in Bun, for some reason slowed down the execution by at least 2 times. To reproduce, let's create 2 file serving HTTP, and loadtest it. ```typescript // sync.ts const handle = () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8080, fetch: handle } // async.ts const handle = async () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8080, fetch: async () => await handle() } ``` Result: ### However, it runs fast if we don't use `await` Let's edit `async.ts` to return the async function **without await**. ```typescript // ? Will not defers const handle = async () => new Response("Hi") export default { port: 8081, fetch: handle } ``` Although, we can work around it by not using `await` keyword or using `Promise.resolve`, it doesn't offer a good Developer Experience, because we can't `unwrap` the value without using then. In the real-world app, the developer will **have to** unwrap the value and performs some action on it. This situation will have the most problem affecting significant performance when using with Bun as HTTP web server. Here's [reproducible repo](https://github.com/SaltyAom/issue-bun-slow-async) if you want to test the problem. ### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition? Always reproducible when using `await` on any platform. ### What is the expected behavior? Bun shouldn't be slowed down by a lot when performing `await` ### What do you see instead? Quote from `What steps will reproduce the bug?` Serving sync, and async server, then perform loadtest, the server is slowed down. However, if we remove `await` but remain `async`, the speed goes up again. ### Additional information The performance slowed down is vary, this problem is tested on: - MacOS with Apple Silicon Chip (M1 Max 32 core) - Darwin Salt.local 21.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.5.0: Tue Apr 26 21:08:37 PDT 2022; root:xnu-8020.121.3~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64 - Slowed down by 2.5x - WSL Debian 11 (AMD Ryzen 5 3500X) - Linux Chiffon 4.19.1280microsoft-standard `#1` SMP Tue Jun 23 12:58:10 UTC 2020 x86_64 GNU/Linux - Slowed down by 1.5x

title: Fix throwing `error: not an error` when calling `db.run(" ")`
body:
Currently `SQLITE_OK` return status from `sqlite3` causes an error to be thrown in several instances (at least potentially). One such instance is when a string that contains only whitespace characters is passed, it ends up not creating a `statement` and so it throws an error saying `not an error` (`SQLITE_OK` result message from `sqlite3` lib). 

We should:
1. Fix instances where `SQLITE_OK` could potentially show up but is not currently checked for.
2. Differentiate between an actual error from parsing a statement and an empty query, and throw an error telling the user the query is probably empty.

Trying to set max listeners of an AbortSignal throws an error.
```js
const ac = new AbortController();

### What is the expected behavior?

As per [node documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#eventssetmaxlistenersn-eventtargets) `events.setMaxListeners` should accept any `EventTarget` as arguments. Since `AbortSignal` [inherits from `EventTarget`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal#instance_properties) setting its max listeners should be supported. body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.6.14

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.4.3-arch1-1 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create file `index.ts`:

```ts
import { fn } from './macro' assert { type: 'macro' };

fn(`© ${''}`); // <-- note the copyright symbol character
```

2. Create file `macro.ts`:

```ts
export function fn(str) {
  return str;
}
```

3. Run `bun build ./index.ts` or `bun ./index.ts`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Template literals are processed correctly as Unicode when passed as macro arguments.
Bun process runs without a segmentation fault.

### What do you see instead?

```
~/P/bun-macro-sigsegv master• ❱ bun build ./index.ts
fish: Job 1, 'bun build ./index.ts' terminated by signal SIGSEGV (Address boundary error)
```

### Additional information

When there is no interpolation in the template literal the macro works as expected, even when it contains non-ASCII characters.

Where there are only ASCII characters, interpolation in the template literal the macro works as expected.

Happens on both stable `v0.6.14 (b5665739)` and current canary `v0.6.15 (c39c11e1)`.

title: Fails to parse ternary expression where parens contain an object with a spread operator

labels.name: bundler
labels.description: Something to do with the bundler

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.6.14

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 22.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun parsing-bug.ts`

```ts
/* parsing-bug.ts */
const a = ({ ...{} }) // ✅
const b = true ? { ...{} } : { ...{} } // ✅
const c = true ? ({ ...{} }) : ({ ...{} }) // ❌
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The expression `true ? ({ ...{} }) : ({ ...{} })` should be parsed by bun.

### What do you see instead?

Bun appears to misinterpret the purpose of the parens and then gets into trouble.

```
error: Expected "=>" but found "..."

const c = true ? ({ ...{} }) : ({ ...{} })
                                  ^
parsing-bug.ts:3:35 95


error: Expected " =" but found "}"

const c = true ? ({ ...{} }) : ({ ...{} })
                                        ^
parsing-bug.ts:3:41 101


error: Unexpected )

const c = true ? ({ ...{} }) : ({ ...{} })
                                         ^
parsing-bug.ts:3:42 102
```

### Additional information

Obviously no formatter would prefer parens in the above cases, but if you were doing something like the following:
```ts
`true ? ({ ...{} } as SomeType) : ({ ...{} } as SomeType)`
```
Formatters like Rome and Prettier do prefer parens for clarity. This situation is how I uncovered the bug.

Also, note that this does not happen with Array syntax, only object syntax.

title: Implement `cp` for `node:fs/promises`
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I've tried completely replacing `node` with `bun` for a [fairly large project](https://github.com/cubing/cubing.js). There were a few incompatibilities that were easy to work around (as well as a general issue running Playwright), but the main thing that's not easy to fix within the project itself was a dependency using `cp` from `fs/promises`: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisescpsrc-dest-options

The function is marked as experimental, but has been available without a flag for two years.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Implement it? 🤓

### What alternatives have you considered?

I can work around this, since I control the build dependency. But I thought I'd report that this was the main thing blocking us from a trivial switchover to `bun` for most of our project!

title: Bun throws error using the cassandra-driver
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

0.7.3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.4.0-105-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Trying to connect to the cassandra database, it this case It's a ScyllaDB one.

```ts
import { Client as ScyllaClient } from "cassandra-driver";
//...
const scyllaClient = new ScyllaClient({
    contactPoints: ['127.0.0.1'],
    localDataCenter: 'datacenter1',
    keyspace: 'my_keyspace',
});

try {
    await scyllaClient.connect();
    logInfo("Connected to ScyllaDB :O")
} catch (error) {
    logError("Error connecting to ScyllaDB >>> ");
    console.log(error);
}
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The application gets connected to the database.

Using node:
```bash
[INFO] >>> Connected to ScyllaDB :O
```

As bun will grow, and new developers come onboard - I've really had a hard time to accept the fact Bun comes with API's accessible through one namespace, for a bunch of unrelated API's.

**Here's a few offending examples:**
```
Bun.serve()
Bun.file()
Bun.write()
Bun.build()
Bun.spawn()
```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Allowing such functionality to be imported or better namespaced.

**Import method**
Currently we have `import('node:fs')`
Perhaps `import('bun:fs')` and use a bun specific api.

**Namespace method**
```
Bun.http.serve()
Bun.fs.open()
Bun.fs.write()
Bun.bundle.build()
Bun.process.spawn()
```

I really feel like the current design will come back to bite everyone in the near future, as well as confuse a lot of people.

title: Use nix to provide single command dev environment setup and reproducible builds
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I want bun to succeed as an open source project. For that to happen, it should be easy for anyone hack on bun’s code base and contribute their improvements back. 

However [the instructions](https://bun.sh/docs/project/development) for setting up dev tooling are not very user friendly.

Image a js project without a `package.json` nor a lock file, which listed it’s npm deps in a README, some with version numbers others without. 

Setting up dev environment for bun should be as easy as running `npm install`. Same for building, testing etc. All deps needed for this should be pinned, just like we do for js projects with lock files.

How? Easy: just use [nix](https://nixos.org/). Drop a [flake.nix (together with flake.lock)](https://zero-to-nix.com/concepts/flakes) in your repo and anyone (on any linux or Mac machine) will be able to run:

1. `nix develop` - to drop into a development shell with all deps needed to build `bun` available and ready to use 
2. `nix build` - to build the `bun` binary (or fetch it from cache if available) 
3. `nix run` - to run the `bun` binary (built from source if a pre-built binary for current state of the repo is not available in local or remote cache)
4. `nix flake check` - to run all checks (tests, lint, format etc) you’d like devs to run before opening a PR

All of these transparently cached and perfectly reproducible.

You might even be able to use this to speed up your CI pipeline ;)

The only requirement for the users would be to install [nix](https://nixos.org/download#nix-install-linux). And hence your development setup instructions could be reduce to 2 lines of bash.

You could even provide a pre-configure instance of [nvim](https://github.com/nix-community/nixvim) or [vscode](https://github.com/nix-community/nix-vscode-extensions) with all tooling (extensions etc) configured and ready to go. 

Finally, for people who really like containers, you could have one built with just a few lines of nix. It would contain the exact same binaries (byte for byte) provided in the dev shell by `nix develop`.



 

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add a [flake.nix](https://zero-to-nix.com/concepts/flakes) defining all dev tools and scripts needed to contribute to bun’s development

### What alternatives have you considered?

Build a docker container with dev environment based on one of the popular distros Linux distros. Meh

Promise 1
Timeout 0
Timeout 1
Immediate 0
Immediate 1

Hello world!
Next tick 0
Next tick 1
Promise 0
Promise 1
Immediate 0
Timeout 0
Timeout 1
Immediate 1

title: AsyncLocalStorage can only be `disable`'d once
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.10+4fbde727d

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 22.6.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The following sample code illustrates the problem that occurs when using AsyncLocalStorage `enterWith()` and `disable()` multiple times within the same process (?):

```js
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "bun:async_hooks"

const store = new AsyncLocalStorage<string>()

store.enterWith("first value")
store.disable()
// This one is correctly undefined:
console.log("first get", store.getStore())

store.enterWith("second value")
store.disable()
// This one should be undefined, but reports "second value" instead!
console.log("second get", store.getStore())
```

### What is the expected behavior?

All calls to `getStore()` after `disable()` should return `undefined`, even when repeated multiple times.

### What do you see instead?

`getStore()` returning the last-stored value instead of `undefined`.

### Additional information

This works as expected in node, so I'm filing an issue instead of doubting my sanity or understanding of AsyncLocalStorage's specification.

title: Broken sourcemaps
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.0.14+d8be3e51b

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.13.0-1022-aws x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a sample file `some-code.ts`:
```ts
console.log("Hello world");
```

2. Build the file and generate sourcemaps with the following script:
```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./some-code.ts"],
  outdir: "./dist",
  target: "bun",
  sourcemap: "external",
});
```

3. Resolve the sourcemap using `sentry-cli`:
```
bunx @sentry/cli sourcemaps resolve dist/some-code.js.map
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The source map should be correctly generated.

### What do you see instead?

The Bun's sourcemap cannot be parsed by tools like `sentry-cli`.

### Additional information

The issue lies in the `mappings` of the source map.

Here's `mappings` generated by Bun for the code in the reproduction:
```
;;AA/////fAAA,QAAQ,IAAI,aAAa;
``` 

The esbuild outputs the following:
```
;AAAA,QAAQ,IAAI,aAAa;
```

I created a [playground](https://codedamn.com/playground/uzX5hjI4bMa8UxZTz0zIw) with some sample source files, 2 bundling scripts using Bun and esbuild, and sourcemap decoder from [this article](https://www.bugsnag.com/blog/source-maps/) ([link to gist](https://gist.github.com/bengourley/c3c62e41c9b579ecc1d51e9d9eb8b9d2))

Run `cat dist-bun/1.js.map | node decode.cjs | jq .` and see the output from Bun's sourcemap:
```json
{
  "version": 3,
  "sources": [
    "../source-samples/1.ts"
  ],
  "sourcesContent": [
    "console.log(\"Hello world\");"
  ],
  "mappings": {
    "1": [
      ""
    ],
    "2": [
      ""
    ],
    "3": [
      "1 => ../source-samples/1.ts -536870910:1",
      "9 => ../source-samples/1.ts -536870910:9",
      "13 => ../source-samples/1.ts -536870910:13",
      "26 => ../source-samples/1.ts -536870910:26"
    ],
    "4": [
      ""
    ]
  },
  "debugId": "076E75C2BF05B11064756e2164756e21",
  "names": []
}
```

The esbuild output is parsed correctly:
```json
{
  "version": 3,
  "sources": [
    "../source-samples/1.ts"
  ],
  "sourcesContent": [
    "console.log(\"Hello world\");"
  ],
  "mappings": {
    "1": [
      ""
    ],
    "2": [
      "1 => ../source-samples/1.ts 1:1",
      "9 => ../source-samples/1.ts 1:9",
      "13 => ../source-samples/1.ts 1:13",
      "26 => ../source-samples/1.ts 1:26"
    ],
    "3": [
      ""
    ]
  },
  "names": []
}
```

Thus Bun's sourcemap is corrupt and cannot be parsed by other tools (I tried `sentry-cli`, but I'm sure others won't work as well).

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.0+5903a6141

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.1-arch1-1 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run the benchmark using node & bun

```
node ./proxy_benchmark.js
vanilla x 1,386,398,241 ops/sec ±1.22% (96 runs sampled)
proxy x 26,280,830 ops/sec ±3.74% (86 runs sampled)
Fastest is vanilla
```

```
bun ./proxy_benchmark.js
vanilla x 48,252,387 ops/sec ±5.82% (63 runs sampled)
proxy x 7,758,912 ops/sec ±2.23% (90 runs sampled)
Fastest is vanilla
```

proxy_benchmark.js
```js
import Benchmark from 'benchmark'
const suite = new Benchmark.Suite
// add tests
suite.add('vanilla', function() {
	const fn = ()=>5
	fn.a = 0
	fn.b = 0
	fn.c = 0
	fn.d = 0
	fn.e = 0
	fn.f = 0
	fn.g = 0
	fn.h = 0
	fn()
}).add('proxy', function() {
	const fn = ()=>5
	const o = {
		a: 0,
		b: 0,
		c: 0,
		d: 0,
		e: 0,
		f: 0,
		g: 0,
		h: 0,
	}
	const proxy = new Proxy(fn, {
		get(_, prop) {
			return o[prop]
		},
		set(_, prop, val) {
			o[prop] = val
			return true
		}
	})
	proxy()
}).on('cycle', function(event) {
	console.log(String(event.target))
}).on('complete', function() {
	console.log('Fastest is ' + this.filter('fastest').map('name'))
}).run()
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun should have around the same performance as Nodejs on the benchmark. Not sure if this is a JavascriptCore vs V8 issue.

### What do you see instead?

Nodejs is >20x faster on the benchmark.

### Additional information

I have not yet verified if this is an issue with the Bun runtime or if this is an issue with JavascriptCore.

title: Prisma in non-awaited async function kills event loop
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.8+89d25807f

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.15.146.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Write a simple code snippet that calls Prisma. Eg.

```js
async function doSomething() {
     console.log("Entry!");
     
     await prisma.someModel.findMany({});
     
     console.log("Exit!")
}
```

Then call this function by a non-awaited call.

```js
doSomething()
``` 

What happens is that the call to Prisma just fizzles out, and it exits the promise at that location. This is not how both regular Node and TS-Node behaves, as they will successfully completely call everything.

### What is the expected behavior?

The entry log should be called, the Prisma function executed, and the exit log should be called

### What do you see instead?

Only the entry log is called, no Prisma call to the database takes place

### Additional information

Does not happen with any other async call (from limited testing), only Prisma

title: CallbackJob prevents VM to exit when result of callback is an unresolved promise
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.10+5102a9443

### What platform is your computer?

Any platform, reproduces everywhere

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This simple code will result in frozen process

```js
setTimeout(() => new Promise(() => 0), 0);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Process exits immediately after setTimeout (which aligns with Node behavior)

### What do you see instead?

Process is stuck. For whatever reason if CallbackJob sees promise, it will subscribe and wait until it succeeds, and this is not always the case.

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/af4e844b621e8c889d2d73c2cd12a7426516ebbf/src/bun.js/api/BunObject.zig#L3811

Potential solution is to deinit CallbackJob regardless of promise status

### Additional information

This bug affects Worker.terminate() - terminate() returns promise which will never complete if Worker is already terminated. #9998 is affected by this bug.

The fact that Worker.terminate() is not fulfilling promise is separate issue. Node fulfills promise every time, but with undefined status code in this case. In attempt to fix original issue's problem I fixed that in #11376

There's also (absolutely irrelevant to this issue, but still notable) difference in status codes - Worker.terminate() yields status code 0 when thread is actually terminated, whereas Node returns 1

title: Brotli support for node:zlib does not respect params (and the default quality setting is unusable for on-the-fly compression)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.10+5102a9443

### What platform is your computer?

Tested on both Ubuntu and Windows

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Using a simple example:
```js
import { createReadStream, createWriteStream } from 'node:fs'
import { createBrotliCompress, brotliCompress, constants as ZLIB } from 'node:zlib'
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises'

const opts = {
	params : {
		[ZLIB.BROTLI_PARAM_MODE] : ZLIB.BROTLI_MODE_TEXT,
		[ZLIB.BROTLI_PARAM_QUALITY] : 4,
	},
}

async function run () {
	await pipeline(
		createReadStream('example.pdf'),
		createBrotliCompress(opts),
		createWriteStream('example.pdf.br'),
	)
	console.timeEnd('pipeline')
}

console.time('pipeline')
run().catch(console.error)
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The params, especially quality (compression level), are applied to compression.

### What do you see instead?

Regardless of params, the size/time ratio is always the same for Bun.

Furthermore, passing any bogus object for the options is accepted, with no error at runtime (Although Bun's TypeScript types are correct, so assuming is stubbed out)

### Additional information

Because `BROTLI_DEFAULT_QUALITY` is 11 (the maximum), this is a serious issue, especially for on-the-fly scenarios where is unusable for me.  E.g. for a 3MB file...

Bun v1.1.10: `[3.83s] pipeline`
v.s.
Node.js v22.1.0: `pipeline: 37.505ms`

(Bun does save slightly smaller file (500KB) to Node's 600KB (where quality level 4 is applied) but that is negligible for **100x slower**!  I've tested without streams and async and is same relative difference.

title: env_loader Map incorrectly implements std.ArrayHashMap in its remove method
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.15-debug+76bd8af3d

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.5.0 x86_64 i386

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The bug has not presented itself, but currently *Map*  in`src/env_loader.zig` implements it's remove method incorrectly:

```zig
    pub fn remove(this: *Map, key: string) void {
        // this.map is a ArrayHashMap
        this.map.remove(key);
    }
```

std.ArrayHashMap has no `remove` method. Only `swapRemove` et al.

### What is the expected behavior?

The custom Map should remove a key.

### What do you see instead?

An error that `remove` does not exist on the underlying std Struct.

### Additional information

This was discovered while I am implementing #11917 and thought it may deserve it's own issue. Will make a PR soon.

body:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

Hi, im trying to create a cli tool for executing .exe file on bun. i'm also trying to create a test for generating random .exe file so that my "validatePath" function could determine if that file path exist or not.

here is my validatePath function code

```javascript
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "bun"

export async function validatePath(path: URL): Promise<URL | string> {

  const filePath = fileURLToPath(path)

  if (await Bun.file(filePath).exists()) {
    return pathToFileURL(filePath)
  } else {
    return ""
  }
}
```

i have two test, the first one test for invalid input

```javascript
test("validate executable given in the config using `validatePath`: invalid value", async () => {

    const filePath = "./sample.exe"

    const newFilePath = await validatePath(pathToFileURL(filePath))

    expect(newFilePath).toBe("");
})
 ```

```javascript
test("validate executable given in the config using `validatePath`: expected real implementation", async () => {

  const editorPath: URL | string = pathToFileURL("./metaeditor64.exe")
  const terminalPath: URL | string = pathToFileURL("./terminal64.exe")

  await Bun.write(editorPath.pathname, "im a editor")
  await Bun.write(terminalPath.pathname, "im a terminal")

  const newEditorPath = <URL>await validatePath(editorPath)
  const newTerminalPath = <URL>await validatePath(terminalPath)

  expect(newEditorPath.pathname).toBe(editorPath.pathname)
  expect(newTerminalPath.pathname).toBe(terminalPath.pathname)
})

```ts
import { beforeAll } from "bun:test"

import { describe, it } from "bun:test"

title: make ci use the `bun.report` code to remap stack traces in PRs
body:
technique to add crash report decoding to bun ci

- test runner thing hosts a server on some port
- spawn all bun instances with the crash reporter environment variable
- the local server handles one url type (`/<code>/ack`)
- it calls `remap` from the bun.report codebase (this can be trivially installed via `bun install` )
- add the remapped stack trace to the CI log

reminder that bun.report is fully self-hostable (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun.report), as well as installable as a package via `bun install`. it also has some helper binaries in `./bin`

specifically ./bin/remap allows --exe to use a custom binary path
```
Usage: remap <trace string> <opts>

Options:
  --md, display as github issue markdown
  --exe, path to executable
```

the code for this program is like 30 lines, most of it being arg parsing. it is a good reference.

title: Memory leak with NestJS and NestJS-graphql
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.21

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.5.0 arm64 arm / Docker with base image oven/bun:1.1.21

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal reproduction repo, with code and documented steps to reproduce:
https://github.com/rskaar/bun-nestjs-graphql-mem-issues

### What is the expected behavior?

The problem occurs when the NestJS app receives requests to any endpoint, as long as the NestJS project has the NestJS-graphQL module imported. For each request, the memory consumption goes up. After 100-300.000 requests, we're at over 1 gb of memory consumption from an initial <100mb.

The same app/code running with NodeJS does not have the same memory leak.

Removing (commenting out) the imported NestJS-GraphQL module gives no memory issues while running.

Note that the requests leading to the memory issues does not need to hit the GraphQL-endpoint. Any traffic to any endpoint in the NestJS app seems to generate a memory leak. I suspect that the NestJS-GraphQL (or ApolloServer) module adds some kind of middleware that each request goes through.

### What do you see instead?

Memory usage goes up for each request and is not garbage collected.

### Additional information

We use Bun in production, and this is a major issue for us - leading to our docker crashing multiple times per day due to memory usage.

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.27+267afa293

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The problem is that breakpoints don't hit if the code contains async functions.

To reproduce, try to debug this sample using `bun-vscode` plugin:

```javascript
console.log('Script started');

async function start() {
    console.log('Starting async function...');
    const test = 'Hello from async function!';
    console.log(test); // breakpoint (ignored)
}

console.log('Starting job...'); // breakpoint (ignored)

start()
    .then(() => console.log(0))
    .catch((e) => {
        console.error('Job failed: ', e);
        process.exit(1);
    })
```

At the same time, if you try to run the same example with WebInspector-based debugger (https://debug.bun.sh) or Safari, all breakpoints hit.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### What do you see instead?

_No response_

### Additional information

Initially, this issue was reported in WebStorm ([YouTrack](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/WEB-68018/Bun-debugger-ignores-breakpoints-in-async-function)).

After some investigation, I found out that the problem lies somewhere in the debug adapter used by the Bun plugins for WebStorm and VS Code.

I had the assumption that it was because `Debugger.resume` [was sent](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-debug-adapter-protocol/src/debugger/adapter.ts#L1466) without awaiting for the future breakpoints to be set. I tried to make a quick fix to check if this was the case, but it turned out that the problem persists.

Here are some examples I used during my investigation: [repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17026578/repro.zip)

- Repro: https://github.com/sebastiansandqvist/trpc-ee-repro

### What is the expected behavior?

The `node:events` `on` function takes a `{ signal }` [option](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#eventsonemitter-eventname-options) which is an `AbortSignal` that should cause the the event listener to deregister. 

### What do you see instead?

When using the `signal` from a request sent over SSE, the event listener is not canceled even after the signal should fire.

### Additional information

https://github.com/trpc/trpc/issues/6045

I've also tried adding the following code to the subscription, which never fires, so perhaps there's something wrong with the request's `AbortController`:

```ts
addAbortListener(signal, () => {
  console.log('aborting');
});
```

title: Memory leak when using Prisma
body:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

I’m using Elysia.js to run an API server that handles approximately 30 requests per second. Over time, I observed an increase in CPU usage, which eventually affects the server’s performance. This issue seems to worsen after making several requests, leading to degraded system performance. Restarting the server temporarily resolves the issue, but this is not a viable long-term solution.

```Dockerfile
FROM oven/bun:1.1.29 AS build
WORKDIR /app
ENV HUSKY=0
COPY package.json bun.lockb ./
COPY ./prisma ./prisma
COPY ./src ./src

# Install dependencies
RUN bun install

# Generate Prisma client with the correct schema location
RUN bunx prisma generate --schema prisma/schema.prisma

# Compile the server to a binary
RUN bun build \
  --compile \
  --minify-whitespace \
  --minify-syntax \
  --target bun \
  --outfile server \
  ./src/index.ts


FROM oven/bun:1.1.29-slim AS runner

WORKDIR /app

# Copy the compiled binary and the Prisma schema from the build stage
COPY --from=build /app/server /app/server
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules/.prisma/client /app/node_modules/.prisma/client
COPY --from=build /app/prisma ./prisma

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y openssl

COPY start.sh /app/start.sh

ENV NODE_ENV=production

RUN chmod +x /app/start.sh

CMD ["/app/start.sh"]
```

## Shell Script (start.sh)
Here is the start.sh script used to start the server:
```
#!/bin/sh

# Run Prisma migrations
echo "Running Prisma migrations..."
bunx prisma migrate deploy --schema prisma/schema.prisma

# Check if the migrations succeeded
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Migrations completed successfully!"
    
    # Start the server
    echo "Starting the server..."
    ./server
else
    echo "Migrations failed. Server will not start."
    exit 1
fi
```

title: cipher doesn't throw an error for invalid argument

body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.1.34+5e5e7c60f

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22621.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Execute JSON.stringify() on an object and see the resulting string.

The object itself doesn't matter... but let's use the following object for example (the same I used while saw this bug):
```javascript
const MY_OBJ = { a: "b" }
```

### What is the expected behavior?

As Node.js do, the expected result should be:

```javascript
JSON.stringify(MY_OBJ);
// Output ==> '{"a":"b"}'
```

### What do you see instead?

Executing the same code into Bun:

```javascript
JSON.stringify(MY_OBJ);
// Output ==> "{\"a\":\"b\"}"
```

### Additional information

TLDR:
- Node.js doesn't escapes double quotes
- Bun escapes automatically double quotes

I think that they should have the same behaviour, in order to don't occur in errors.

title: sourcemap without sourcesContent field
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I have a source map generated with the following code:
```ts
await Bun.build({
    // ...
    sourcemap: "linked"
})
```

Through both [this tool](https://github.com/ampproject/remapping) or manually, if I remove the `sourcesContent` field from the source map, but fails to decode the source map giving a `InvalidSourceMap` when an error occurs in the built file.

I want line numbers and file names in my errors but need to remove any actual src code from the source map and to reduce build size as well.

I can see in bun, this behavior isn't allowed ([here](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/cc125b475f7035cb793d59382a56ac2597224964/src/sourcemap/sourcemap.zig#L153)) but in the [source map format specification](https://tc39.es/ecma426/#source-map-format), it is allowed, this makes it impossible to have just line numbers and file names as I'm requesting.

Furthermore, with source content removed from the source map, this section (see image below) should be removed from errors because if code is minified (and is all on one line now), it makes the error huge but only the file and line number is needed.

(an example with sourcemap with sourcesContent, just showing which section)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd016ac2-410e-42b3-b979-a9d17e5de4b9)


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Allow for source maps without the sourcesContent field, whilst keeping line number and filenames

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_

title: Keep AsyncLocalStorage context across bun:test test cases
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I am writing a somewhat low-level util method for my backend service that relies on AsyncLocalStorage for Dependency Injection. When I want to test services that rely on this method, I want to create the AsyncLocalStorage store from a `beforeEach` or `beforeAll` method, maybe even a global `setup` file. However, in each individual test case, it seems like that context is gone (the store resolves to undefined).

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

not really a new feature - the test runner should ideally work in a way where it keeps context across the **entire** test run lifecycle

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_

title: Support to run scope command without `run` command
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

So I have a `package.json` like this:

```json
{
   "scripts": { "pack": "bun build", "test:todo": "bun test --todo" }
}
```

For `pack` command, I can simply run this `bun pack` and it works nicely. But for command with scope `test:todo`, `bun test:todo` is not working only this work `bun run test:todo`. I think it doesn't make sense.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Could we support `bun test:todo`? (and other characters such as `.`, `!`, `[`, `]`, `+`)

### What alternatives have you considered?

Or we can create a shortcut binary for `bun run` like `bunr` that means for running only package script command?


> actually I did this in machine, quite good - recommend this:
> 
> ```bash
> #!/usr/bin/env bash                                                                                           
> bun run $@
> ```
> 
> with `sudo chmod 751 bunr`

title: Truncated stack trace when awaiting a promise before throwing an error
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.2.4 & 1.2.5-canary.47+078318f33

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.3.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When I throw an error in an async function, the stack trace correctly includes the full call stack, showing the sequence of function calls leading to the error. However, if an `await` statement (e.g., `await Promise.resolve(true)`) is added before throwing the error in the same async function, the resulting stack trace becomes incomplete. Specifically, it omits critical details about the call hierarchy, reducing the stack trace to only the line where the error is thrown, without referencing the calling function(s).

**Steps to Reproduce:**

```ts
async function throwError() {
  throw new Error();
}

async function run() {
  await throwError();
}

run();
```

Expected stack trace (correct):

```
Error: 
      at <anonymous> (/redacted/path/to/index.ts:3:9)
      at throwError (/redacted/path/to/index.ts:1:26)
      at <anonymous> (/redacted/path/to/index.ts:7:9)
      at run (/redacted/path/to/index.ts:6:19)
      at /redacted/path/to/index.ts:10:1
```

Modify the throwError function to include an await:

```ts
async function throwError() {
  await Promise.resolve(true); // Added this line
  throw new Error();
}

async function run() {
  await throwError();
}

run();
```

Actual stack trace (truncated):

```
Error: 
      at <anonymous> (/redacted/path/to/index.ts:3:9)
```

⚠️ It also says `<anonymous>`, when it's not.

⚠️ _**This is an oversimplified repro, but the issue occurs in a large project where callers are in different files. No way to trace who called the throwing method in question.**_

### What is the expected behavior?

The stack trace should consistently include the full call stack, including the `run` function and the invocation of `throwError`, regardless of whether an await is present in `throwError`.

FWIW, Node also truncates the stack but it _still includes_ the caller:

```
Error
    at throwError (/redacted/path/to/index.js:3:9)
    at async run (/redacted/path/to/index.js:7:3)

Node.js v23.8.0
```


### What do you see instead?

When an `await` is added to `throwError`, the stack trace is truncated, showing only the line where the error is thrown (`throw new Error()`) and omitting the calling context (e.g., `run` and the initial call to `throwError`).

### Additional information

_No response_

title: 76+ Second DNS Resolution Delay with Google Maps Geocoding API
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.2.13+64ed68c9e

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 21.6.0 x86_64 i386

### What steps can reproduce the bug?


I'm using the Google Maps Geocoding API, which responds quickly (~120ms per the server-timing header). However, the initial fetch request in Bun takes over 70 seconds. Timing tests with console.time('fetch') and console.timeEnd('fetch') confirm the delay occurs during the fetch request itself. 
I suspect Bun struggles with DNS resolution for maps.googleapis.com. After the initial DNS lookup is cached, subsequent requests are fast (~180ms), indicating the issue is specific to Bun's initial DNS handling.




Make a fetch request to the Google Maps Geocoding API:

```ts
import * as nodeDns from "node:dns";

nodeDns.setServers(['8.8.8.8', '8.8.4.4']);

console.time('fetch');
const response = await fetch(`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?key=[your-key]&address=[address]`);
console.timeEnd('fetch');
```

First request takes ~70+ seconds.
Subsequent requests (with cached DNS) take ~180ms.
```ts
[70.12s] fetch  // Initial request
[1.23ms] json
[0.87ms] parse
[182.45ms] cache

[90.45ms] fetch  // Cached request
[0.32ms] json
[0.19ms] parse
[179.12ms] cache
```



Works for subsequent requests but doesn't fix initial delay.
Relying on DNS caching for fast subsequent requests, but the initial 70-second delay is slow.

body:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

## 🐛 Bug Report: ` { isAsyncFunction } from  "node:util/types"` crashes Bun when used on `.bind()`ed functions

### What’s happening?

When using `isAsyncFunction` from `node:util/types`, Bun crashes with a segmentation fault if the argument is a function that was bound using `.bind()`.

This does **not** happen in Node.js, and it affects both class methods and regular functions when bound to any object.

---

### Works fine

```ts
import { isAsyncFunction } from "node:util/types";

function normalFn() {}
console.log(isAsyncFunction(normalFn)); // false
```

---

### Crashes Bun

```ts
import { isAsyncFunction } from "node:util/types";

const obj = { fn: null as any };

obj.fn = function () {
  console.log("this should not crash");
}.bind(obj);

console.log("Before isAsyncFunction call");
isAsyncFunction(obj.fn); // ❗ Segmentation fault in Bun
console.log("After isAsyncFunction call");
```

---

### Environment

* **Bun Version**: v1.2.16, v1.2.17 and  v1.2.18
* **OS**: Linux (tested on x64 / glibc)
* **Crash**: Segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) on `isAsyncFunction(boundFn)`

---

### Notes

* The crash happens consistently across runs.
* A bound function (even if not async) causes the crash.
* Native Node.js | Deno handles this correctly without crashing.
* Likely linked to Bun’s internal function tag inspection in `node:util/types`.

     * `true` and `false` are aliases for `"inline"` and `"none"`, respectively.
     *
     * @default "none"

     * @see {@link outdir} required for `"linked"` maps

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This occurs inconsistently in a migrated Node.js application using Bun. The error is thrown and caught normally within the application, but the stack trace output sometimes appears malformed or incomplete. This happens sporadically in the same location, where most of the time the stack traces are correct.

Unfortunately, due to the complexity of the app and the non-deterministic nature of the issue, creating a minimal reproduction case is likely not feasible.

Here is an example of a broken stack trace:
```bash

    at va (/$bunfs/root/ambient-core:1082:208)

    at new va (/$bunfs/root/ambient-core:1082:208)
    at handleIncomingResponse (/$bunfs/root/ambient-core:1092:11185)

    at new va (/$bunfs/root/ambient-core:1082:208)
    at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/ambient-core:1092:5018)

In the broken examples:
- The error name (`AmbientClientException`) and message are missing or replaced with a generic `Error`.
- The number of stack trace entries is inconsistent or truncated.
- The `new` keyword is sometimes omitted from the constructor call in the trace.

### What is the expected behavior?

- The correct error name and message.
- All expected at lines in the stack trace.
- Proper formatting (including the new keyword where applicable).


### What do you see instead?

- Generic Error shown instead of the custom error class name and message.
- Incomplete or truncated stack traces.
- Missing or malformed constructor information.

### Additional information

- The issue occurs randomly but always in the same function call.
- This app was recently migrated from Node.js to Bun.

title: Maximum call stack size exceeded with Hono v4.9.4 in minimal setup
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.2.21

### What platform is your computer?

 macOS (Darwin 24.6.0, arm64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

  1. Create a new directory and run `bun init`
  2. Install Hono v4.9.4: `bun add hono@4.9.4`
  3. Create server.js with minimal Hono app:

  ```javascript
  import { serve } from 'bun';
  import { Hono } from 'hono';

  const app = new Hono();

  app.get('/health', (c) => {
    return c.json({ status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() });
  });

  const port = parseInt(process.env.PORT || '3000');
  const server = serve({
    port,
    fetch: app.fetch,
  });

  console.log(`Server running on http://localhost:${port}`);
  export default server;

  4. Run: bun server.js
  5. Test any endpoint: curl http://localhost:3000/health

### What is the expected behavior?

HTTP requests should return JSON responses:
  - GET /health should return: {"status":"ok","timestamp":"2025-08-28T01:18:20.083Z"}
  - Server should handle requests normally (sans current error)


### What do you see instead?

All HTTP requests fail with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" error.

  Instead of JSON, requests return an HTML error page with:
  - Title: "GET - /health failed"
  - Error: "ExceptionOccurred" → "RangeError" → "Maximum call stack size exceeded"
  - No stack trace or useful debugging information

  The server starts successfully but every single HTTP request triggers this stack overflow.

### Additional information

Root Cause: This appears to be a runtime compatibility issue between Bun's serve() function and Hono v4.9.4's internal
  architecture.

  Evidence:
  - Same code works perfectly with Node.js + @hono/node-server
  - Issue persists with absolutely minimal Hono apps (no middleware, no external dependencies)
  - Tested with latest Bun v1.2.21 - issue still occurs
  - Works fine with Hono v3.x

  Workarounds:
  - Downgrade to Hono v3.x: bun add hono@3
  - Use Node.js runtime instead of Bun
  - Switch to Bun-native frameworks like Elysia

title: Bun's microtask queue with `vm.runInContext` behaves different than Node.js
Implement Linked AsyncContextFrame for AsyncLocalStorage performance
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

## Update: Issue was caused by benchmarking debug builds, not release builds

**TL;DR: The performance issue reported does not exist in release builds. All benchmarks were inadvertently run using `bun bd test` (debug build) instead of release builds. Bun's AsyncLocalStorage in release builds is actually faster than Node.js.**

### Corrected Benchmark Results (Release Builds)

**Basic Operations (1M iterations)**

| Operation             | Node.js v24.7.0 | Bun v24.3.0 (release) | Winner            |
| --------------------- | --------------- | --------------------- | ----------------- |
| **run() overhead**    | 0.167 μs        | **0.041 μs**          | **Bun 4x faster** |
| **enterWith()**       | 0.125 μs        | **0.041 μs**          | **Bun 3x faster** |
| getStore() empty      | 0.000 μs        | 0.000 μs              | Tie               |
| getStore() with value | 0.000 μs        | 0.000 μs              | Tie               |

**Deep Nesting Performance**

| Test                        | Node.js  | Bun (release) | Bun Advantage    |
| --------------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ---------------- |
| Deep nesting (5 levels)     | 2.333 μs | 0.125 μs      | **18.6x faster** |
| Deep nesting (10 levels)    | 6.041 μs | 0.209 μs      | **28.9x faster** |
| enterWith() 3 ALS instances | 1.375 μs | 0.041 μs      | **33.5x faster** |

### What Went Wrong

The original benchmarks showing "321x slower" and "518x slower" were run using debug builds:

| Metric      | Debug Build | Release Build | Debug Slowdown |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| run()       | 149.291 μs  | 0.083 μs      | 1,800x slower  |
| enterWith() | 144.333 μs  | 0.042 μs      | 3,436x slower  |

The debug build numbers (134-149 μs) closely match what was reported in the original issue. Debug builds are expected to be extremely slow due to:

- No compiler optimizations (-O0)
- Debug symbols and assertions
- Extensive logging and instrumentation
- Not representative of production performance

### Conclusion

- ✅ Bun's AsyncLocalStorage in **release builds** is production-ready
- ✅ Bun is **3-33x faster than Node.js** across realistic workloads
- ❌ The claimed "55x slowdown" does not exist in production
- ❌ This is **not** blocking OpenTelemetry support

My apologies for the confusion and wasted time. Lesson learned: Validate Claude benchmark outputs by hand, in a fresh environment, without lingering documentation/specs or dangling ttys. 

---

## Implement Linked AsyncContextFrame for AsyncLocalStorage performance

### Problem

Use of AsyncLocalStorage causes severe performance degradation in Bun due to array cloning overhead. With OpenTelemetry instrumentation ([pr24063](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/24063), addressing #3775), HTTP throughput drops from **110k req/s** (no context) to **2k req/s** (with context) - a 55x slowdown. Support for this was added to bun in #1832 ([pr3089](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/3089)) using a zero-cost-when-unused strategy of manually wrapping callsites in zig. However, Bun's current implementation (`src/js/node/async_hooks.ts`) uses a flat array `[als1, value1, als2, value2, ...]` that is cloned twice per `run()` call to maintain immutability. This creates O(n²) overhead with nested contexts. The additional copying and object creation overhead drastically impacts performance.

This is blocking production-ready OpenTelemetry support in Bun in environments which require distributed tracing. It basically precludes Bun from being a viable choice of runtime for any meaningful traffic volume.


### Benchmark Results - Inaccurate

**Basic Operations**

| Operation                   | Bun (median)      | Node.js (median) | Ratio            | Impact              |
| --------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------- |
| **new AsyncLocalStorage()** | 2.625 μs          | 0.042 μs         | 62.5x slower     | Low - one-time cost |
| **getStore() empty**        | 0.166 μs          | 0.000 μs         | ~∞               | Low - still fast    |
| **getStore() with value**   | 0.167 μs          | 0.041 μs         | 4.1x slower      | Low - acceptable    |
| **run() overhead**          | **134.083 μs** ⚠️ | **0.417 μs**     | **321x slower**  | **CRITICAL**        |
| **enterWith()**             | **129.459 μs** ⚠️ | **0.250 μs**     | **518x slower**  | **CRITICAL**        |
| **exit()**                  | **255.666 μs** ⚠️ | ~0.5 μs\*        | **~500x slower** | **CRITICAL**        |

\*Node.js exit() estimated based on run() overhead

**Scaling Behavior**

| Scenario             | Bun      | Node.js  | Analysis                     |
| -------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| **Nesting Depth 20** | 0.166 μs | 0.000 μs | Bun maintains constant time  |
| **20 ALS instances** | 0.292 μs | 0.041 μs | Bun: 1.7x growth, Node: 1.0x |
| **Multiple reads**   | Linear   | Linear   | Both scale well              |

**Async Context Propagation**

| Operation            | Bun       | Node.js   | Ratio       |
| -------------------- | --------- | --------- | ----------- |
| **Promise.then()**   | 6.750 μs  | 1.667 μs  | 4x slower   |
| **async/await (3x)** | 76.042 μs | 44.791 μs | 1.7x slower |
| **setTimeout**       | 1,172 μs  | N/A       | Very slow   |
| **setImmediate**     | 32.250 μs | N/A       | Moderate    |

### Claude's Analysis

**Bun** stores ALS in a flat array:

```
[als1, 'value1', als2, 'value2', ]
```

To be able to recover after `value2` is set, the entire array must be copied before the call.

To prevent mutation after, the array is copied again before persisting it. There is a clone on every `enterWith`!

```javascript
// Current implementation
run(store_value, callback, ...args) {
    let context = get();
    context = context!.slice();  // Clone #1 (~100μs)
    // ... modify ...
    try {
        return callback(...args);
    } finally {
        context = get()!.slice();  // Clone #2 (~100μs)
        // ... restore ...
    }
}
```

This additional copying is slow and creates significant GC pressure. 


- Current implementation: `src/js/node/async_hooks.ts`
- Native wrapper: `src/bun.js/bindings/AsyncContextFrame.{cpp,h}`
- Related: #3775 (OpenTelemetry support), [PR #24063 OTel instrumentation](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/24063)

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

### Possible Solution: Parent-Linked AsyncContextFrame (Node.js v24)

Node.js v24 implemented frame-based inheritance via [PR #55552](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/55552), aligned with the [TC39 Async Context proposal](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context), that replaces the map (or array, in Bun) cloning with parent-pointer frame hierarchy.

**JavaScript layer** (`lib/internal/async_context_frame.js`):

```javascript
class AsyncContextFrame extends SafeMap {
  constructor(store, data) {
    super(AsyncContextFrame.current()); // Inherit from parent via Map
    this.set(store, data);
  }
}
```

**C++ layer** (`src/async_context_frame.cc`, `src/async_context_frame.h`):

- Thin wrapper around V8's `isolate->GetContinuationPreservedEmbedderDataV2()`
- Automatic propagation for Promises via V8 engine

**Frames form a tree structure**:

```
ROOT (empty)
  │
  ├─> Frame1 [ALS1: 'value1']
  │     │
  │     ├─> Frame2 [ALS2: 'value2']
  │     │     └─> Frame3 [ALS1: 'updated']  // Shadows parent's ALS1
  │     │
  │     └─> Frame4 [ALS3: 'value3']
  │
  └─> Frame5 [ALS1: 'other']
```

With shadowing, overwriting `value1` --> `updated` in Frame 3 does not require cloning the entire context, just a fallback lookup algorithm (`get(key): this?.Map.get(key) ?? this?.parent?.get(key)`)

**Benefits**:

- **O(1) frame creation** (just pointer to parent)
- **Copy-on-write**: only allocate on modification
- **Automatic GC**: frames cleaned up when no longer referenced
- **100-300x faster** than array-based approach
- The frame-based approach is also more semantically correct: async contexts naturally form a hierarchy, and the data structure should reflect that.

**Refs**
- [Async Context Proposal](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context)
- [PR #55552: AsyncContextFrame implementation](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/55552)
- [`lib/internal/async_context_frame.js`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/async_context_frame.js)
- [`lib/internal/async_local_storage/async_context_frame.js`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/async_local_storage/async_context_frame.js)
- [`src/async_context_frame.cc`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/src/async_context_frame.cc)
- [`src/async_context_frame.h`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/src/async_context_frame.h)

### What alternatives have you considered?

1. Turn off distributed tracing by default. However, this is a core feature of observability stacks, and will probably be turned back on.  
2. Use the opentelemetry c++ library and only instrument native operations; leave opentelemetry-js out of it. But we want to be node compatible, right?
3. Hardcore patching JWC to provide something like `SetContinuationPreservedEmbedderData()`. Seems hard, and was (maybe) rejected by the original ALS/async_hooks authors.

title: Allow setting install backend in bunfig
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I want to be able to globally set the install backend to `symlink` due to the particular way the filesystem on my machine is set up. Basically, I want this:

```
~/my-proj/node_modules/path/to/dep/file.js -> ~/.cache/.bun/install/cache/path/to/dep@version/file.js
```

Currently, bun is using hardlinks instead of symlinks, which is problematic in my setup.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

I'd like the ability to set the install backend in `~/.config/.bunfig.toml`:
```toml
[install]
backend = "symlink"
``` 

### What alternatives have you considered?

Running `bun install --backend=symlink` does what I want. I just want to be able to set this option in my global bunfig.

Longer reproduction:

I added console.log calls line 34-36 below for debugging purpose:

```js
'use strict'

var dotenvExpand = function (config) {
  // if ignoring process.env, use a blank object
  var environment = config.ignoreProcessEnv ? {} : process.env

  var interpolate = function (envValue) {
    var matches = envValue.match(/(.?\${?(?:[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)?}?)/g) || []

    return matches.reduce(function (newEnv, match) {
      var parts = /(.?)\${?([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)?}?/g.exec(match)
      var prefix = parts[1]

      var value, replacePart

      if (prefix === '\\') {
        replacePart = parts[0]
        value = replacePart.replace('\\$', '$')
      } else {
        var key = parts[2]
        replacePart = parts[0].substring(prefix.length)
        // process.env value 'wins' over .env file's value
        value = environment.hasOwnProperty(key) ? environment[key] : (config.parsed[key] || '')

        // Resolve recursive interpolations
        value = interpolate(value)
      }

      return newEnv.replace(replacePart, value)
    }, envValue)
  }

  for (var configKey in config.parsed) {
    console.log('[line 34] dotenv-expand: ignoreProcessEnv:', config.ignoreProcessEnv)
    console.log('[line 35] typeof environment:', typeof environment)
    console.log('[line 36] typeof environment.hasOwnProperty:', typeof environment.hasOwnProperty)
    var value = environment.hasOwnProperty(configKey) ? environment[configKey] : config.parsed[configKey]

    config.parsed[configKey] = interpolate(value)
  }

  for (var processKey in config.parsed) {
    environment[processKey] = config.parsed[processKey]
  }

  return config
}

module.exports = dotenvExpand

title: `String.raw` corrupts null bytes in template literals
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.10+30e609e08

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create `test.js` with a literal null byte (0x00) between the backticks:
```js
const s = String.raw``;
console.log("length:", s.length);
console.log("charCode[0]:", s.charCodeAt(0));
```

Run with `bun test.js` and `node test.js`.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
length: 1
charCode[0]: 0
```

A null byte in a template literal should be preserved as-is, matching Node v22.22.0 behavior.

### What do you see instead?

```
length: 6
charCode[0]: 92
```

Bun outputs the 6-character literal string `\uFFFD` (`\`, `u`, `F`, `F`, `F`, `D`) instead of a single null byte.

### Additional information

Bun version: `1.3.10+30e609e08`  
Node version: `v22.22.0` (reference)

Ran into this with [`wasm-audio-decoders`](https://github.com/eshaz/wasm-audio-decoders), which uses [`simple-yenc`](https://github.com/eshaz/simple-yenc) to embed WASM binaries as yEncoded strings in template literals, decoded at runtime via `String.raw`. Every decoder (`mpg123-decoder`, `flac`, `ogg-vorbis`) failed with a CRC mismatch because null bytes in the payload were being corrupted by the transpiler.

Workaround was applied in simple-yenc (escape null bytes on encode, treat `0xFFFD` as `0x00` on decode) but the root cause is in Bun.

title: `node:test` async tests and hooks time out after 5s instead of matching Node.js no-timeout default
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.10+30e609e08

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```javascript
import { it, before } from 'node:test';

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

before(async () => {
  await sleep(7000); // setup taking 7 seconds
});

it('long async test', async () => {
  await sleep(7000);
});
```

Run with `bun test file.test.mjs`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node.js output:
```
✔ long async test (7008ms)
```

In Node.js, `node:test` has no default timeout. Tests and hooks run until they complete.

### What do you see instead?

Bun output:
```
✗ long async test [5000.08ms]
  ^ this test timed out after 5000ms, before its done callback was called.
```

Two problems:

1. **Wrong timeout**: `node:test` tests and hooks inherit bun:test's 5s default instead of Node.js's no-timeout default.
2. **Misleading error message**: The error says "done callback was called" even though the test uses async/await, not done callbacks.

### Root cause

In `src/js/node/test.ts`, both `createTest` and `createHook` wrap the user's function with a `(done) => {}` callback pattern. Since `fn.length === 1`, bun:test interprets this as a done-callback-style test and applies its 5-second default timeout. Neither wrapper sets `timeout: 0` to match Node.js's no-timeout semantics.

The same issue affects hooks (`before`, `after`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`) — they also use the done-callback wrapper pattern and never forward timeout options to the underlying bun:test hook functions.

### Additional information

Related to #27422. This also affects hooks, not just tests.

```bash
TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'isLikelyComponentType' of 'k' as it is undefined.
    at V0 (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at b.reactRefreshAccept (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at src/frontend/hooks/useAuth.tsx (useAuth.tsx:80:8)
    at CY (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at m (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at nY (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at m (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at nY (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at m (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
    at nY (Bun HMR Runtime:1:1)
```

### Additional information

This is the new Rust port. Downgrading to latest stable 1.3.14 works fine.  turning of hmr seems to work fine as well.

According to claude:

````
What's happening
The crash is inside Bun's bundled HMR runtime (_bun/client/index-…js), not in your app code. The stack trace shows:

reactRefreshAccept is called when [useAuth.tsx](vscode-webview://1o8bbiti2dnen65hvrjqesbci9e9tkbnr3rmhu8lcen2jru0akin/src/frontend/hooks/useAuth.tsx) is hot-updated.
Internally it calls V0(k) and destructures const { isLikelyComponentType } = k.
k is the React-Refresh runtime module reference — and Bun is passing undefined.
isLikelyComponentType is an export of react-refresh/runtime. Bun ships its own bundled copy of that runtime inside the HMR client. In 1.3.14 (your new canary) that internal hookup is broken — the runtime reference resolves to undefined, and the destructure throws on the first file the bundler tries to wrap with Fast Refresh.
````

title: fs.promises.statfs returns misaligned struct on darwin-x64 (bsize=0, fields shifted)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 x86_64 (macOS on Intel)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
import fs from "node:fs";
const s = await fs.promises.statfs("/");
console.log(s);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Same values as Node.js on the same machine:

```js
{
  type: 26,
  bsize: 4096,
  blocks: 488475719,
  bfree: 473415905,
  bavail: 473415905,
  files: 4292221443,
  ffree: 4291794580
}
```

### What do you see instead?

```js
{
  type: 0,
  bsize: 0,                 // should be 4096
  blocks: 4096,             // should be 488475719  (this is bsize value)
  bfree: 1048576,           // should be 473415905
  bavail: 488475719,        // should be 473415905  (this is blocks value)
  files: 473415902,
  ffree: 473415902
}
```

The fields look shifted by one slot, suggesting the struct layout used to decode the macOS `statfs64` syscall is misaligned on `darwin-x64`. With `bsize=0`, any consumer that computes `blocks * bsize` reports zero available space.

### Additional information

- `darwin-arm64` is **unaffected** — same Bun version on M-series Macs returns the correct values.
- Both `darwin-x64-modern` and `darwin-x64` baseline compile targets reproduce.
- Confirmed against Node.js on the same volume — Node returns the expected values, so this is Bun-specific, not a kernel quirk.
- Downstream impact: hit in Unity Hub CLI — every disk-space pre-check on Intel Macs failed with "not enough space" because the underlying `statfs.bsize` was 0. Workaround in place via a `df -Pk` fallback until this is fixed.

title: Map/Set lose distinct integer keys ≥ 2^31 on 1.4.0-canary (regression)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+b3d086e26

### What platform is your computer?

WSL

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

# `Map` and `Set` merge distinct integer keys ≥ 2³¹  (canary 1.4.0 regression)

## What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.0-canary.1` -- revision `b3d086e26f3a6fc39733316d7af7b1d661fe81c6` (`oven/bun:canary`).

Every stable release tested is **unaffected**: `1.3.5`, `1.3.13`, `1.3.14`, `latest`.
This is a regression on the `1.4` line.

## What platform is your computer?

`Linux x64 (baseline)` -- WSL2, kernel `6.6.87`, glibc `2.41`.
Also reproduced cleanly in the official `oven/bun:canary` Docker image, so it is not
environment-specific.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const a = 1779314400000; // a millisecond timestamp
const b = 1779400800000; // a different timestamp, one day later

console.log(a === b); // false -- these are two distinct numbers

const m = new Map();
m.set(a, "A");
m.set(b, "B");

console.log(m.size);   // 1   ← expected 2
console.log(m.get(a)); // "B" ← expected "A"
console.log(m.get(b)); // "B"

console.log(new Set([a, b]).size); // 1 ← expected 2
```

`Map` and `Set` treat **every integer-valued number key with magnitude ≥ 2³¹** as the
same key. It is not just a hash-bucket collision -- the keys compare *equal*, so
membership is wrong too:

```js
const m = new Map([[2 ** 40, "only-key"]]);
console.log(m.has(2 ** 41)); // true ← expected false (never inserted)
```

## What is the expected behavior?

`m.size === 2`, `m.get(a) === "A"`, `new Set([a, b]).size === 2`,
`m.has(<never-inserted-key>) === false` -- i.e. distinct numbers are distinct keys.
This is what Node.js, every browser, and every stable Bun release do.

## What do you see instead?

The second `set()` overwrites the first. `get()` / `has()` on any large-integer key
resolve to the most-recently-inserted large-integer entry. All large-integer keys
behave as a single equivalence class.

## Additional information

### Boundary -- the defect starts exactly at 2³¹ (the signed 32-bit limit)

| Key | canary 1.4.0 |
|-----|--------------|
| integers in `[-(2³¹-1), 2³¹-1]` | ✅ correct |
| integers `≥ 2³¹` | ❌ all merge into one key |
| integers `≤ -2³¹` | ❌ all merge into one key (incl. `INT32_MIN`) |
| non-integer doubles (e.g. `2³² + 0.5`) | ✅ correct |
| plain object property keys | ✅ correct |

```js
new Map([[2 ** 30, 1], [2 ** 30 + 1, 2]]).size  // 2  ok
new Map([[2 ** 31, 1], [2 ** 31 + 1, 2]]).size  // 1  BUG
new Map([[2 ** 32, 1], [2 ** 33, 2], [2 ** 34, 3]]).size  // 1  BUG (all three merge)
```

- A small (in-range) integer never collides with a large one -- `0` vs `2³²` stay
  distinct. Large integers only collide *with each other*.
- Non-integer doubles take a different, correct path; only **integer-valued** numbers
  are hit.

### Regression matrix

| Bun | revision | result |
|-----|----------|--------|
| `1.3.5`  | `1e86cebd74a5723e818b5c0555276b646bcf0e4c` | ✅ correct |
| `1.3.13` | `bf2e2cecf27e800962b1e7f03d66278f9d5d2e79` | ✅ correct |
| `1.3.14` | `0d9b296af33f2b851fcbf4df3e9ec89751734ba4` | ✅ correct |
| `1.4.0-canary.1` | `b3d086e26f3a6fc39733316d7af7b1d661fe81c6` | ❌ **bug** |

### Likely cause

The boundary is exactly 2³¹ and non-integer doubles are unaffected, which suggests the
new (`1.4`) `Map`/`Set` implementation has an integer key fast-path that only handles
`i32`, and the fallback for integers outside that range produces both a constant hash
**and** a broken key-equality comparison.

### Real-world impact

This is not a contrived case. It surfaced as a production bug where a dashboard
aggregated values into a `Map<number, Bucket>` keyed by a period `Date.getTime()`.
Every `Date.now()` value (~`1.7e12`) is in the broken range, so all buckets collapsed
into one and every period reported the grand total. Keying a `Map`/`Set` by a timestamp
is an extremely common pattern.

### Reproduction

Two `docker run` commands -- no local Bun needed, only the image tag differs:

```sh
# stable -- prints "Map size: 2" (correct)
docker run --rm oven/bun:latest bun -e 'const m = new Map([[2**32, "a"], [2**33, "b"]]); console.log("size", m.size, "get(2**32)", m.get(2**32))'

# canary -- prints "Map size: 1" (bug)
docker run --rm oven/bun:canary bun -e 'const m = new Map([[2**32, "a"], [2**33, "b"]]); console.log("size", m.size, "get(2**32)", m.get(2**32))'
```

---

*Possibly separate issue:* on the same canary build, running a script located at the
filesystem root (`bun /script.mjs`) panics with
`panic: cannot resolve DirInfo for non-absolute path`. Stable Bun runs it fine. This is
unrelated to the `Map` bug and may warrant its own report.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

# What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create `repro.mjs`:

```js
await new Promise(() => {})
```

Run it with Bun:

```sh
bun repro.mjs
```

For comparison, run the same file with Node:

```sh
node repro.mjs
```

# What is the expected behavior?

Bun should match Node parity for unsettled top-level await: print a warning and exit with a non-zero status instead of keeping the process alive indefinitely.

Node 24.14.1 prints:

```text
Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await at file:///.../repro.mjs:1
await new Promise(() => {})
^
```

and exits with status 13.

# What do you see instead?

`bun repro.mjs` produces no output and remains running indefinitely.

This was reproduced with:

```text
bun --revision
1.3.14+0d9b296af

node --version
v24.14.1
```

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.12.86+deb13-amd64 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Hi,

I would like to report a behavior in Bun that can be reproduced using the below snippet:
```javascript
if (typeof setImmediate !== 'function') {
  throw new Error('setImmediate is not defined in this runtime. Provide a polyfill for Deno or your environment before running this test.');
}
const immediate = setImmediate(() => {});
console.log('immediate._onImmediate =', immediate._onImmediate);
console.log(typeof immediate._onImmediate);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
root@KContainer:~/5767# node a.mjs
immediate._onImmediate = [Function (anonymous)]
function
```

### What do you see instead?

```
root@KContainer:~/5767# bun run a.mjs
immediate._onImmediate = undefined
undefined
```
_onImmediate is not a spec requirement, but is used by Node-based test suites and internal inspection logic.
